meta.purpose: Single machine-readable source of truth for implementing the SOPHEP Recruitment Management System. Contains every decision, correction, constraint and requirement agreed during design.
notes_for_implementers: Anything marked corrects_v1_error replaces an earlier design that was WRONG. Do not implement the v1 form.
Requirements using 'shall' are mandatory. Absence is a defect.
Where this JSON and prose documents disagree, treat it as a defect in this JSON and raise it.

project.name: SOPHEP Recruitment Management System
project.problem: Manage society induction end to end: application, check-in, queueing, interviewing, scoring, department allocation, offers.
project.scale_design_target: 1000 applicants per cycle without architectural change
project.cadence: Two cycles per year (Spring, Fall), reused every semester
in_scope: Registration via online, walk-in digital, walk-in paper transcription
Applicant identity, access tokens, QR codes
Event-day check-in including full offline operation
Queue management, panel assignment, no-show handling
Structured interview evaluation with bias correction
Role-based access control and append-only audit

out_of_scope.reason: PWA meets all needs at lower cost
Separate system; RMS exports a roster

out_of_scope.item: Automated CV parsing or ML ranking
out_of_scope.reason: Fairness risk disproportionate to benefit at this scale
Schema accommodates it; not implemented this release

glossary.definition: One complete induction round, e.g. Spring 2027. Top-level container for all data.
A scheduled phase within a cycle: Registration, Interview Day 1, Review, Decisions.
A queue lane. Usually one per department, or a single shared 'general' track.
A session: the set of interviewers occupying a room for a shift. The unit that PULLS from the queue.
A physical location. Deliberately distinct from Panel.
Period after an applicant is called before they are marked skipped. Default 5 minutes.
Removed from the active queue after repeated non-attendance; requires manual reactivation.
Empirical-Bayes correction of interviewer strictness. w = n/(n+5).
An action requiring confirmation by two DISTINCT authenticated Super Admins.
A derived field written only by the owning transition function, in the same transaction.
Gale-Shapley applicant-proposing stable matching used for department allocation.

design_principles.detail: Every critical path has a degraded mode. No single failure - network, server, device, person - may halt registration or interviewing.

design_principles.principle: Never present a number you know is stale as if it were live
design_principles.detail: Honesty beats the appearance of stability. Promoted to a principle because v1 violated it (see errata E11).

design_principles.principle: Every state change is atomic, idempotent, and audited
design_principles.detail: Retrying must never produce a second effect. Every decision affecting a person traces to a human and a timestamp.
Every piece of state has exactly one owner. Projections are written in the same transaction as their source.

design_principles.principle: Fairness is enforced by the schema, not by policy
design_principles.detail: Bias controls live in the database and permission model, not in asking people to behave.
Enforced at row level in the database, never by UI alone.

design_principles.principle: Optimise for the fifteen seconds at the desk
design_principles.detail: A volunteer under pressure completes check-in in one scan and zero decisions.
Departments, rubrics, criteria, stages, capacities and templates are data. A new cycle never requires a deployment.
Historical data is a record, not a working document.

errata.description: Fifteen defects found in the v1 design during self-audit. Each entry describes what was wrong, why, and the correction. Implementers must build the corrected form.

items.title: Offline QR verification was cryptographically broken
items.v1_design: QR carries an HMAC signature; check-in device verifies it offline using 'the cycle HMAC public verification parameters'.
items.why_wrong: HMAC is symmetric. There is no HMAC public verification parameter. Verifying HMAC requires the signing secret itself, so v1 required shipping the cycle QR signing secret to every volunteer phone. Anyone extracting it could mint unlimited valid SOPHEP QR codes.
items.correction: Primary offline verification is sha256(token) set-membership against the cached roster - no cryptography and no secret required. Ed25519 (asymmetric) signature added ONLY to cover applicants registered after the morning roster sync; devices hold the PUBLIC key only.

items.title: Normalisation scale and score thresholds contradicted each other
items.why_wrong: That mapping forces cohort mean 50, sd 10 by construction. So 75 is +2.5 sigma, roughly the top 0.6 percent - auto-shortlist would fire for about one person in 200. The 55-75 manual band would swallow around 30 percent of the cohort, about 60 people, in a meeting described as covering 29. Thresholds calibrated for a raw 0-100 scale were silently applied to a z-scale.
items.correction: Map to the cohort distribution, not an arbitrary 50/10. Express selection thresholds relative to department capacity as ranks, not absolute scores.

items.title: Averaging raw and normalised scores together is meaningless
items.v1_design: Interviewers with fewer than 8 evaluations fall back to raw; then final = mean(normalised across all evaluations).
items.why_wrong: Two different scales averaged together. Also creates a cliff: an interviewer's 8th evaluation retroactively rescales the previous seven, so identically-scored applicants rank differently based on how many OTHER people their interviewer saw.
items.correction: Empirical-Bayes shrinkage. One formula always applied: w = n/(n+5), bias = interviewer_mean - cohort_mean, adjusted = raw - (w * bias). Continuous, never mixes scales, no mode switch. The sigma >= 3 guard from v1 is deleted as unnecessary.

items.title: Unique index on email made the documented override path impossible
items.v1_design: Prose allowed dedupe override with a reason; schema declared a plain UNIQUE index on (cycle_id, email_norm).
items.why_wrong: The override INSERT would fail on constraint violation. Prose and schema directly contradicted; a documented flow branch was forbidden by the database.
items.correction: Add dedupe_override_reason column. Partial unique index excludes rows where dedupe_override_reason IS NOT NULL. Accidents still caught; deliberate audited overrides work.

items.title: Two sources of truth for applicant state
items.v1_design: applicants.state and queue_entries.state both encoded queued/called/in_interview with nothing keeping them consistent.
items.why_wrong: They would drift. First symptom: an applicant whose status page and panel screen disagree, during the event, in front of them. Unfixable after the fact because nothing records which was right.
items.correction: Explicit state ownership. queue_entries.state is authoritative for event-day state; applicants.state is a projection written in the same transaction by the same function only.

items.title: email_norm was a no-op that did not match its own description
items.v1_design: email_norm citext GENERATED ALWAYS AS (lower(email)) STORED, on a column already typed citext.
items.why_wrong: citext is already case-insensitive, so lower() did nothing. Prose promised Gmail dot and plus-tag stripping the column never implemented, so a.b+induction@gmail.com and ab@gmail.com were treated as different people when v1 explicitly said they would not be.
items.correction: Real IMMUTABLE norm_email() and norm_phone() functions used by the generated columns.

items.title: NOT IN in the queue claim recusal filter
items.v1_design: AND applicant_id NOT IN (SELECT applicant_id FROM recusals WHERE ...)
items.why_wrong: NOT IN returns ZERO rows if the subquery yields a single NULL. On the floor this looks like the system silently stopped handing out applicants - a total queue stall with no error. Also the slower plan.

items.title: Deferred acceptance was non-deterministic
items.v1_design: Departments ranked applicants by score plus a recommendation bonus. Ordering stopped there.
items.why_wrong: Scores tie frequently on a coarse rubric. Running allocation twice could produce two different valid stable matchings. In a dispute, 'the algorithm decided' is only a defence if the algorithm decides the SAME thing every time.
items.correction: Total deterministic tie-break chain: adjusted score desc, recommendation count desc, panel spread asc, application time asc, applicant_id asc.

items.title: RLS depended on a session variable that never gets set under a pooler
items.v1_design: Policies read current_setting('app.applicant_id', true); nothing said how it is written.
items.why_wrong: Under transaction-mode connection pooling (Supabase default) a session-level SET either leaks across unrelated requests or vanishes. Either the security boundary fails open, or nothing works.
items.correction: Derive from verified JWT claims, or set_config(..., true) inside the same transaction. Policies use nullif(...)::uuid so an unset context yields NULL and matches nothing - fails closed.

items.title: Panel state machine could not represent blocked
items.v1_design: panels.status enum was closed | open | busy | break.
items.why_wrong: The design described panels unable to call next until all evaluations were in, but there was no state for it. An unrepresentable state is one the UI has to guess at.

items.title: Wait-time clamp was designed to display a number known to be false
items.v1_design: Never let the estimate increase while the applicant's queue position has not worsened.
items.why_wrong: If two of four panels break, the true wait doubles with position unchanged. The rule would keep showing the old, now-wrong number - prioritising the appearance of stability over telling someone the truth about their afternoon.
items.correction: Revise upward whenever active_panels or observed service time changes materially, and always state the cause.

items.title: Overstated registration throughput
items.v1_design: Claimed the per-cycle counter sustains thousands of registrations per second.
items.why_wrong: The row lock serialises ALL registrations for a cycle. Honest figure is a few hundred per second, bounded by commit latency. The overstatement undercut the credibility of the 10,000-applicant scaling claim.
items.correction: State honest numbers; document the sharded counter alternative in the scale path.

items.title: Permission gate assumed a single role per user
items.v1_design: memberships PK permitted several roles per user per cycle, but the gate loaded one role.
items.why_wrong: A Coordinator who also interviews - entirely normal - would be silently denied their second role's capabilities.
items.correction: Effective capabilities are the UNION across all roles held in that cycle, computed once at session start. No deny rules.

items.title: No timezone policy
items.v1_design: All timestamptz, but every '10:00' in the spec was ambiguous.
items.why_wrong: Stage boundaries, grace windows and display times would be implemented inconsistently across clients.
items.correction: Store timestamptz. Each cycle carries an IANA timezone, default Asia/Karachi. All rendering derives from it. Never persist local wall-clock strings.

items.title: Undefined behaviour when a stage closes with interviews running
items.why_wrong: Orphaned in_interview and awaiting_evaluations records; the classic failure of discovering eleven missing evaluations three days later when interviewers no longer remember the candidates.
items.correction: Stage close is a hard gate: blocks on in_progress interviews, blocks on outstanding evaluations with a per-interviewer waiver action, warns on queued/called with bulk carry-forward or no-show, then auto-resolves parked to no_show.

domain_model.hierarchy: Society > Cycle > {Stage, Department, Track, Room, Panel, Rubric, Applicant, Notification, AuditEvent}

entities.name: Society
entities.purpose: Top-level owner. Enables future multi-society tenancy.

entities.name: Cycle
entities.purpose: One induction round. Container for everything.

entities.name: Stage
entities.purpose: Scheduled phase; gates which operations are legal.

entities.name: Department
entities.purpose: Destination with a capacity and interviewers.

entities.name: Track
entities.purpose: Queue lane. Decouples queueing from department structure.

entities.name: Panel
entities.purpose: A SESSION of interviewers in a room. The unit that pulls from the queue.

entities.name: Rubric
entities.purpose: Versioned criteria set with weights and anchors.

entities.name: Applicant
entities.purpose: A person applying in this cycle.

entities.name: AccessToken
entities.purpose: Bearer credential for QR and status page. Stored hashed.

entities.name: CheckIn
entities.purpose: Owner of the checked-in fact. One per applicant per stage.

entities.name: Interview
entities.purpose: One panel session with one applicant.

entities.name: Evaluation
entities.purpose: One interviewer's scoring of one interview. Immutable on submit.

entities.name: AuditEvent
entities.purpose: Append-only record of every state change.

critical_distinction.reason: Interviewers rotate, take breaks and swap rooms. Without a Panel entity every rotation corrupts throughput statistics and the audit trail.

domain_model.why_track_exists: A single queue routes a Logistics applicant to a Design panel that cannot evaluate them, while Logistics interviewers sit idle. Recommended default for SOPHEP scale: one 'general' track for round 1; per-department tracks only if a second round is introduced. Schema supports both from day one.

state_ownership.rule: Every fact has exactly one owning table. applicants.state is NEVER written directly by application code.
invariants: Every transition function writes an audit_events row in the SAME transaction. No audit, no commit.
A nightly job re-derives applicants.state from owners and alerts on any mismatch. Drift is monitored, not mysterious.

transitions.guard: interview stage active AND token valid AND not already checked in for this stage
panel open AND panel serves track AND no recusal

transitions.trigger: all evaluations submitted OR coordinator waiver
transitions.guard: every panel member submitted or waived
results locked by two distinct super admins
still eligible and not placed elsewhere

transitions.effect: DELETE queue entry in same transaction

applicant.rejection_behaviour: Any transition not listed returns HTTP 409 INVALID_TRANSITION with current_state and attempted in the detail object.

transitions.trigger: panel resumes on a replacement device

panel.notes: awaiting_evaluations blocks the Call Next action. The UI must state WHICH interviewer is outstanding - a disabled control without explanation is a defect (FR-INT-013).

cycle.role: Global gate checked by EVERY write endpoint, not the UI.

transitions.guard: stage close gate passed - see stage_close_gate
President locks AND General Secretary confirms, distinct users
unlock requires dual control plus reason

cycle.archived_behaviour: Read-only at the DATABASE level. No hard-delete endpoint exists for any child record.

stage_close_gate.rationale: Blocking is deliberate. The alternative is discovering eleven missing evaluations three days later, when interviewers no longer remember the candidates.

checks_in_order.response: List blocking interviews by room and panel
List outstanding evaluations grouped by interviewer, with a per-row waive action
Coordinator waives that specific evaluation with a written reason; audited; interview completes on remaining evaluations
List them; offer bulk carry-forward to next interview stage or bulk no-show
Parked applicants auto-resolve to no_show; write audit event; close stage

parts.meaning: Season: SP Spring, FA Fall, SU Summer

applicant_id.why_not_user_original: The user's original SP26-0001 used SP for SOPHEP, so Spring 2026 and Fall 2026 produced identical prefixes. Two cycles in one year collided semantically and staff could not tell cycles apart by eye.
generation_sql: -- Inside the SAME transaction as the applicant INSERT
applicant_id.forbidden_pattern: SELECT MAX(sequence) + 1 -- produces duplicate IDs the first time two desks register simultaneously. Reject at code review (FR-IDT-003).
applicant_id.honest_throughput: A few hundred registrations per second, bounded by commit latency. Roughly 100x realistic peak. v1 claimed thousands - see errata E12.

token.storage: sha256(token) ONLY. Raw token never persisted in any database, log or backup.
token.signature_rationale: Asymmetric. Devices hold the PUBLIC key and can verify without being able to sign. HMAC could never do this - that was the v1 flaw.
token.qr_payload_rationale: A full HTTPS URL means any phone camera opens the status page as a fallback. The custom scanner is an optimisation, not a dependency.

verification_layers.name: Format
verification_layers.catches: Garbage and other apps' QR codes

verification_layers.name: Roster hash
verification_layers.catches: Everyone registered before sync - the 99 percent case

verification_layers.name: Ed25519
verification_layers.catches: Applicants registered after the morning roster sync

verification_layers.name: Server
verification_layers.catches: Revocation, wrong cycle, wrong state, already used

rules: Exactly one active token per applicant; rotation revokes the previous immediately and atomically
Lookups rate-limited to 10 per minute per source IP
Cycle keypair rotated per cycle, so a prior cycle's QR fails verification
Tokens expire 60 days after final decisions

registration.unification_rule: Paper is an INPUT METHOD, not a separate pipeline. One code path, one set of edge cases, one thing for a volunteer to learn under pressure. The volunteer transcribes into the same entry screen; the paper original is filed with the applicant ID written top-right.
registration.why_changed_from_user_design: User's original gave QR only to online applicants, creating two divergent check-in paths and a second-class experience for walk-ins.

signals.normalisation: lowercase, trim; for gmail.com and googlemail.com only, strip dots and plus-suffixes from local part
final 9 digits after removing all non-numeric characters

hard_block_resolutions.effect: Jump to check-in for the existing record
Set dedupe_override_reason (min 10 chars), write audit event, proceed

deduplication.soft_warning_behaviour: Dismissible in one tap. Never blocks.

slot_booking.rationale: The classic induction failure is 200 people arriving at 10:00 for a process serving 20 per hour; the last person waits eight hours and half leave. Slot booking turns arrivals from Poisson into schedulable, which is the difference between an orderly hall and a corridor full of resentful students. It also makes wait estimates dramatically more accurate.

cv_upload.serving: signed URLs, 15 minute max TTL, generated per request, each generation audited, Content-Disposition attachment

check_in.target: Under 8 seconds end to end, ZERO taps on the success path
check_in.camera_behaviour: Continuously active. NOT a press-to-scan button.
check_in.success_behaviour: Auto-dismiss after 2.5 seconds. No confirmation tap - across 200 scans that is 200 chances to double-tap and 200 wasted seconds.
check_in.failure_behaviour: Requires explicit dismissal. A failure that scrolls past unnoticed becomes a person nobody checked in.

branches.rationale: It is the most common non-happy path, it is NOT an error, and a red screen in front of a nervous applicant reads as 'you have a problem' when the correct message is 'you are fine'.

branches.volunteer_action: combined flow, under 30 seconds, flags needs_completion
search by any 4 digits of ID, last 4 of phone, or partial name

branches.system_action: enqueue, SUPPRESS ETA, raise ops alert

offline.local_storage: IndexedDB, client-generated UUID plus device timestamp
offline.indicator: Persistent amber banner WITH diagonal stripe pattern - colour is never the only signal

reconnect.mechanism: each operation carries its original Idempotency-Key; server deduplicates via idempotency_keys table
reconnect.conflict_resolution: earliest server-received timestamp wins; conflict is LOGGED, never silently discarded

hard_fallback.artefact: Printed roster sorted by ID and by surname, with tick boxes
hard_fallback.recovery: Coordinator bulk-reconcile screen accepting a list of identifiers
hard_fallback.policy: Print every morning. You will probably never use it, and the one time you do it will save the event.

check_in.timestamp_authority: Server timestamps are authoritative for ALL business logic. Client timestamps are persisted separately and used only for replay ordering.

queue_engine.why_not_push: Push assignment goes stale the moment one interview overruns. The system tells applicant 33 'Room 2' while Room 2 is 20 minutes behind and Room 4 sits empty. The display and the volunteer's manual reassignment then disagree.
claim_sql: AND NOT EXISTS (            -- was NOT IN: NULL-unsafe, could stall the queue (E7)
ORDER BY q.priority DESC, q.enqueued_at ASC
queue_engine.atomicity_guarantee: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Ten panels can press Call Next in the same millisecond and each receives a DIFFERENT applicant - no application-level locking, no retries, no possibility of double assignment. Zero rows returned means the queue is genuinely empty.

priority_tiers.label: Interview voided through no fault of theirs

queue_engine.priority_philosophy: Priority is DATA, not code. Coordinators can adjust any entry with a mandatory reason, visible in the audit log. Floor managers WILL need to bump someone; a system that forbids it is a system they stop using.

grace_extension.trigger: applicant taps 'I'm on my way' on their status page
grace_extension.rationale: A 5-minute hard timer skips people who are 30 seconds away. Each avoided skip is an argument that never happens at the desk.

first_skip.rationale: A SOFT penalty. Sending someone from position 3 to position 40 over a two-minute absence provokes an argument at the desk that costs more time than the delay did.

second_skip.effect: removed from panel-visible queues, added to volunteer worklist

empty_queue_with_parked.behaviour: Panel interface shows the parked count; volunteers alerted to locate them
empty_queue_with_parked.rationale: Otherwise panels idle while people sit fifteen metres away.

no_show_handling.panel_idle_time_after_skip: zero seconds - the skip and the next claim are the same transaction boundary

formula.active_panels: panels with status open or busy on that track
formula.eta: ceil(position / max(active_panels,1)) * service_ewma + remaining time on the in-flight interview

display_rules.rule: Always a RANGE, never a single number
display_rules.rationale: A single number is read as a promise, and every broken promise costs trust

display_rules.rule: Revise UPWARD when the truth changes and state the cause
display_rules.example: Two panels are on break - about 15 minutes longer
display_rules.rationale: v1 suppressed upward revision and would have displayed a number it knew was wrong

display_rules.rule: Suppress entirely for the first 15 minutes of a stage
display_rules.rationale: The EWMA has no data; 'We will call you shortly' is more honest and more useful

display_rules.rule: Suppress whenever the track has no open panel
display_rules.rationale: Otherwise the applicant waits on a fictional estimate

display_rules.replacement: You're next / Almost your turn - stay nearby
display_rules.rationale: Precision there is impossible and unnecessary

wait_estimation.connection_loss_behaviour: Keep the last known number visible with an explicit timestamp. NEVER a bare spinner - blanking the screen on someone in position 3 is cruel.

interviewer_must_not_see: Any other interviewer's scores or remarks, including from a previous round
Any aggregate, average, rank or percentile
interview.concealment_enforcement: Row-level database policy, NOT the user interface alone.

rubric.scope: per cycle, optionally overridden per department
rubric.weight_constraint: must sum to exactly 100, enforced by database constraint

anchors.minimum: at least min and max scale values
anchors.rationale: An unanchored 1-5 scale means five different things to five interviewers, and no statistical normalisation fully recovers from that. Written anchors are the cheapest fairness intervention available.

version_pinning.rationale: Otherwise an edit mid-session splits one panel across two scales
version_pinning.corrects_v1_error: E10 related, documented in ARCH v2 section 9.2

submission.revision_behaviour: Creates a NEW revision with mandatory reason; original retained; audit log holds both
submission.after_window: Super Admin unlock only, itself audited
submission.completion_gate: Interview completes only when EVERY panel member has submitted, or a Coordinator waives a specific outstanding evaluation
submission.blocking_effect: Panel cannot Call Next while awaiting_evaluations
submission.blocking_rationale: This is what prevents the classic end-of-day discovery that eleven evaluations were never submitted

deadlock_escape_hatch.requires: written reason identifying the waived interviewer
deadlock_escape_hatch.rationale: Without this, one interviewer going home permanently disables a panel for the rest of the day

submission.validation: Submit disabled until every criterion is scored, with unscored criteria marked INLINE at the point of omission, not by a single error at the bottom

heartbeat.on_threshold: interview transitions to flagged and appears on the operations dashboard

recusal.who_may_declare: any interviewer, against any applicant, at any time
recusal.enforcement: honoured by the queue claim query - a recused interviewer's panel is simply never offered that applicant

auto_suggest.behaviour: PROMPT only, never an automatic action

recusal.rationale: Student societies are small. An interviewer will encounter their roommate.

ui_rules: No view change without explicit user action
An interviewer mid-sentence must never have the screen change under them

bias_correction.why_needed: If Interviewer A averages 4.2 and Interviewer B averages 2.8 across the same population, an applicant's fate depends substantially on which door they walked through.

formulas.cohort_mean: mean of raw across EVERY evaluation in the cycle

bias_correction.scale_invariant: adjusted stays on the SAME 0-100 scale as raw, so the two are directly comparable and thresholds keep their plain meaning

shrinkage_table.effect: Almost none - one data point proves nothing about strictness

deleted_from_v1: The sigma >= 3 guard - unnecessary under shrinkage
bias_correction.computed_when: review time, against the full distribution - NOT at submission

scoring.applicant_final_score: mean of adjusted across all evaluations of that applicant
scoring.display_rule: Both raw AND adjusted shown side by side wherever scores are presented. The review meeting must see what actually happened, not only what the maths concluded.

flags.condition: adjusted score spread across a panel exceeds 20 points
flags.rationale: Disagreement is not a bug - it is exactly the case where a human decision adds the most value, and where an automatic average silently splits the difference and hides the problem

flags.condition: any criterion scored 2 or below on a 5-point scale
flags.effect: auto-exclude regardless of rank, subject to manual override

flags.condition: every evaluator of this applicant has fewer than 5 evaluations

review_bands.basis: rank within department, RELATIVE TO CAPACITY - not absolute score
review_bands.why: Absolute cutoffs need recalibrating every cycle and were miscalibrated in v1. Rank scales automatically to any cohort size.
review_bands.worked_example: For an 8-place department: ranks 1-6 clear, 7-16 discussed, 17+ below. Roughly 10 discussions per department - a review meeting that actually finishes.

allocation.problem_statement: Design has 8 places and 30 qualified applicants. Media has 6 places and 4 applicants. Applicant 42 preferences Design first, Media second, and ranks 11th in Design.
allocation.why_not_greedy: Filling each department greedily by score produces unstable outcomes - applicant 42 gets nothing while Media stays empty, and someone Design rejected would have been Media's top pick.

preflight_gates.gate: Every interview is complete or explicitly voided
Every active department has a capacity set
No other allocation holds the advisory lock

allocation.applicant_preferences: their ranked department choices from the application form

chain.criterion: count of interviewer 'recommend for this department'

department_ordering.why_levels_4_and_5: They are arbitrary, and that is the point. They make the ordering total, so the algorithm returns an identical result every run. v1 stopped at level 1 and could produce different results on re-runs, which is indefensible when someone asks why they ranked below a person with the same score.

loop: Each unmatched applicant proposes to their highest-ranked department that has not yet rejected them
Each department provisionally holds its top `capacity` proposals by its own ordering and rejects the rest

outcomes.detail: ranked per department using the same ordering

outcomes.result: below the line or criterion floor

properties: Stable - no applicant-department pair would both rather have each other
Explainable - for any outcome you can name which department rejected them and why
Deterministic - byte-identical results on repeated runs over unchanged input
Fast - milliseconds at any scale this system will reach

override.effect: new decision version, original retained, audited
override.philosophy: The algorithm proposes; humans decide. But the default is defensible and the overrides are visible.

steps.constraint: MUST be a different authenticated user; the same session cannot do both

outputs: verification that no selected applicant lacks a department

steps.effect: status pages update; emails dispatch through rate-limited queue

publication.corrections_policy: Post-publication corrections NEVER mutate the snapshot. They create a new versioned decision and a distinct correction notice. The record of what was published stays intact - which is what you want the first time someone disputes a result.

cascade_steps: Take the top-ranked waitlisted applicant for that department
Verify still eligible and not placed elsewhere; if not, mark lapsed on the waitlist and take the next
Send offer with a fresh expiry clock
Notify Super Admins and write an audit event

stop_conditions.rationale: near the end of a cycle you may want to close a department rather than keep cascading

matrix.content: ID, QR, status link, what happens next
Arrival window, venue, what to bring
We called and missed you - see the desk

implementation_rules: All outbound mail goes through an asynchronous QUEUE with retry and per-provider rate limiting. Never send in the request cycle - a slow provider must not block a check-in.
Store per-recipient delivery state; consume webhooks for delivered, bounced, complained
Bounces surface on the ops dashboard as actionable items. On results day, an undelivered result is a person who does not know their outcome.
Every template is data, previewable, and versioned. Never hardcode email copy.
Suppression list respected absolutely, except for transactional result notices.
notifications.sms_note: Worth adding later for the position <= 3 nudge only. That single message eliminates most no-shows because it reaches people who wandered off for coffee. Not needed for v1.

roles.rationale: On the day, someone must reorder the queue, reassign panels and resolve stuck interviews WITHOUT being able to see a single score. The Volunteer role cannot bump a priority; the Admin role is a data role that should not be firefighting. Separating floor authority from scoring visibility is the entire point.
Read-only across everything including scores, write access nowhere. Being able to grant full visibility without granting any power is what makes disputes resolvable.

multi_role.rule: Where a user holds multiple roles in one cycle, effective capabilities are the UNION across all roles, computed once at session start.
multi_role.deny_rules: None exist. A capability is either granted by some role or absent. Keeps the model composable and avoids 'why can't I do this, I'm an admin' ambiguity.

enforcement_layers.role: The real boundary. An interviewer's connection cannot read another interviewer's evaluation rows regardless of what the API asks.
Every endpoint declares a required capability; shared middleware enforces it and returns 403 with a machine-readable reason.
Hides what the user cannot do. ERGONOMICS ONLY. Never treat as security.

dual_control.rule: Two distinct authenticated Super Admin accounts. The same session cannot complete both steps.
dual_control.rationale: Ten extra seconds removes an entire category of 'who published this' from your society's future.
dual_control.db_constraint: CHECK (lock_confirmed_by IS NULL OR lock_confirmed_by <> locked_by)

realtime.principle: Real-time is a LAYER, not a foundation. It keeps the UI fresh; it is never the source of truth. Postgres is.

channels.payload: called IDs and room, waiting count
flags, stuck interviews, sync failures, bounces

realtime.channel_security_note: Channel design is a security boundary. The display channel physically cannot carry a name because the PUBLISHER never puts one there - you are not trusting a client to omit it.

degradation_ladder.behaviour: automatic reconnect, exponential backoff 1s, 2s, 4s, capped at 30s
fall back to polling every 5s; Reconnecting indicator plus last-updated time
offline mode; cached data with explicit timestamp; writes queue locally
printed roster and paper queue slips; bulk reconcile on recovery

realtime.honesty_rule: Never show stale data as if it were live. Every real-time surface carries a connection indicator and a last-updated time. An applicant who knows the number is 3 minutes old is fine; an applicant who trusts a frozen number and misses their call is not.

role_specific_offline.behaviour: queue writes to IndexedDB, verification runs locally
cache evaluation locally, block Call Next
show stale timestamp, never a fabricated live number

idempotency.mechanism: Every mutating request carries a client-generated Idempotency-Key
idempotency.same_key_same_hash: replay the stored response without re-executing
idempotency.value: This single mechanism makes the flaky-network double-tap harmless and makes offline replay safe by construction.

failure_matrix.mitigation: Per-cycle counter incremented in-transaction

failure_matrix.scenario: Two volunteers scan the same QR at once
failure_matrix.unhandled_consequence: Two check-in records, doubled queue entry
failure_matrix.mitigation: Idempotency key + UNIQUE(applicant_id, stage_id) + state guard

failure_matrix.scenario: Two panels press Call Next simultaneously
failure_matrix.unhandled_consequence: Same applicant sent to two rooms
failure_matrix.mitigation: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED - structurally impossible
Same idempotency key on both taps; second replays the first response
UNIQUE(interview_id, interviewer_id); second submit enters the revision flow

failure_matrix.scenario: Applicant registers online then walks in
failure_matrix.mitigation: Dedupe on normalised email, phone, roll
Heartbeat every 30s; 90 min silence flags it; Coordinator voids or force-completes; void requeues at priority 100
Optimistic local write; UI states 'pending' explicitly, never 'done'
Server timestamps authoritative; client timestamps stored separately for replay ordering only

failure_matrix.unhandled_consequence: Panel idles waiting for a ghost
failure_matrix.mitigation: Grace window then skip then park
Recusal, honoured in the claim query

failure_matrix.scenario: Results published with a wrong email
failure_matrix.mitigation: Delivery tracking via webhooks; bounces on the ops dashboard for manual follow-up

failure_matrix.scenario: Super Admin publishes early by mistake
failure_matrix.mitigation: Dual control + dry-run preview + typed confirmation + re-authentication
Immutable published snapshot; corrections are new versions
ARCHIVED cycles read-only in the database; soft delete only; no hard-delete endpoint exists

failure_matrix.scenario: QR screenshot shared between two students
failure_matrix.unhandled_consequence: One person interviewed under another's ID
failure_matrix.mitigation: One active token per applicant; single-use check-in; second scan shows the earlier time and the desk sees the mismatch

failure_matrix.unhandled_consequence: Scores measured on different scales, silently
failure_matrix.mitigation: Rubrics versioned; each evaluation records rubric_version_id pinned at interview START

failure_matrix.unhandled_consequence: Half the applicants receive results, half do not
failure_matrix.mitigation: Outbound queue with retry, per-provider rate limiting, per-recipient delivery state

failure_matrix.scenario: Two Super Admins run allocation concurrently
failure_matrix.mitigation: Advisory lock on allocation:{cycle_id}; second run rejected

failure_matrix.scenario: Interviewer forgets to submit at end of day
failure_matrix.mitigation: Panel blocked + ops counter + stage-close gate

failure_matrix.unhandled_consequence: Panel disabled for the rest of the day
failure_matrix.mitigation: Coordinator waiver with reason
NOT EXISTS instead of NOT IN - errata E7

failure_matrix.unhandled_consequence: Applicants wait on a fictional ETA
failure_matrix.mitigation: Detected at check-in; ETA suppressed; ops alert raised

failure_matrix.scenario: Stage closed with interviews still running
failure_matrix.mitigation: Stage-close gate blocks and lists them

capacity_model.purpose: Run BEFORE the event. The single most common planning failure.
capacity_model.utilisation_rationale: Accounts for changeovers, no-shows, breaks and overruns. Planning at 1.0 is how every induction day runs three hours late.
capacity_model.ui_requirement: Build as a screen. Super Admin enters expected applicants, interview length and available panels; system returns required hours, a feasibility verdict, and the minimum panel count for the available window. Then derives time-slot capacities from the same numbers.
capacity_model.why_it_matters: Discovering infeasibility a week ahead is a planning decision. Discovering it at 14:00 on the day is a crisis.

data_model.migration_note: Real migrations create users before cycles and add circular references (cycles.locked_by) as deferred constraints. Tables below are grouped by concern for readability, not dependency order.

norm_email: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION norm_email(addr text) RETURNS text
norm_phone: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION norm_phone(p text) RETURNS text
normalisation_functions.effect: A.B+induction@Gmail.com and ab@gmail.com now genuinely collide, as v1 claimed but never implemented.

tables.name: cycles
constraints: CHECK (lock_confirmed_by IS NULL OR lock_confirmed_by <> locked_by)
tables.notes: qr_private_key_enc is KMS-encrypted and NEVER leaves the server (errata E1)

tables.name: memberships
tables.notes: Multiple rows per user per cycle are legal; capabilities are the UNION (errata E13)

tables.name: applicants
indexes: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_applicant_email ON applicants (cycle_id, email_norm) WHERE state NOT IN ('withdrawn','screened_out') AND dedupe_override_reason IS NULL
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_applicant_phone ON applicants (cycle_id, phone_norm) WHERE state NOT IN ('withdrawn','screened_out') AND dedupe_override_reason IS NULL
CREATE INDEX idx_applicant_name_trgm ON applicants USING gin (full_name gin_trgm_ops)
tables.notes: Partial indexes fix errata E4 - the plain UNIQUE index made the documented override path impossible

tables.name: access_tokens
key_columns: token_hash bytea unique -- sha256, raw NEVER stored
indexes: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_active_token ON access_tokens (applicant_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL

tables.name: check_ins
tables.notes: server_timestamp is authoritative; client_timestamp is for offline replay ordering only

tables.name: panels
tables.purpose: A SESSION of interviewers in a room

tables.name: queue_entries
constraints: CHECK (priority_reason IS NOT NULL OR priority IN (5,10,30,50))
indexes: CREATE INDEX idx_queue_claim ON queue_entries (cycle_id, track_id, priority DESC, enqueued_at) WHERE state = 'waiting'
tables.notes: The partial index is what makes the claim query fast at any scale

tables.name: interviews
tables.purpose: One panel session with one applicant

tables.name: rubrics
key_columns: department_id fk NULLABLE -- NULL means cycle default

tables.name: criteria
tables.notes: Weights must sum to 100 across a rubric, enforced by trigger. Anchors are MANDATORY.

tables.name: evaluations
key_columns: rubric_id fk -- pinned at interview START
constraints: CHECK (waived_by IS NULL OR waiver_reason IS NOT NULL)

tables.name: decisions
constraints: CHECK (allocation_method <> 'manual_override' OR override_reason IS NOT NULL)

tables.name: result_snapshots
tables.notes: Write-once. Corrections create new decision versions, never mutate this.

tables.name: audit_events
indexes: CREATE INDEX idx_audit_entity ON audit_events (entity_type, entity_id, created_at DESC)
constraints: REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_events FROM PUBLIC

rls.binding_problem: Under a transaction-mode connection pooler (Supabase default), a session-level SET either leaks across unrelated requests or vanishes. Either the boundary fails open or nothing works.

supported_patterns.method: set_config inside the SAME transaction with is_local = true

rls.fail_closed_rule: Policies use nullif(current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::uuid. If unset, the value is NULL and every comparison is NULL - zero rows. The boundary fails CLOSED, the only acceptable direction.

policies.name: eval_privileged
policies.sql: USING (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memberships m JOIN interviews i ON i.id = evaluations.interview_id WHERE m.user_id = nullif(current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::uuid AND m.cycle_id = i.cycle_id AND m.role IN ('super_admin','auditor')))

rls.value: With these in place, 'interviewers cannot see each other's scores' is a property of the DATABASE. A frontend bug cannot leak it; a rushed endpoint cannot leak it.

time_policy.forbidden: Never store local wall-clock strings. Stage boundaries are absolute instants; '10:00' in any UI is a rendering of one.

api.idempotency: Every mutating endpoint requires an Idempotency-Key header
api.authorisation: Every endpoint declares a required capability, enforced by shared middleware

endpoints.purpose: Resolve token to status page payload
Polling fallback for the live view
Desk lookup by ID, name, phone, roll
Offline bundle - hashes plus public key
Counts plus sample emails plus validation

api.external_dependency_rule: No external service may sit in the SYNCHRONOUS path of check-in, queue claim or evaluation submission.

authentication.method: Token URL, no account; optional emailed OTP to view results

at_rest: qr_private_key_enc and totp_secret_enc additionally encrypted at the application layer with a KMS-held key
security.key_rule: The Ed25519 PRIVATE key never leaves the server. No private key material is transmitted to any client device under any circumstance.

rate_limits.limit: 5 attempts per 15 minutes per account, progressive backoff

hardening: Bot protection on the public form (Turnstile or equivalent)
Secrets in a manager, never in the repository
Dependency vulnerability scan on every build, critical findings fail the build
All inputs validated server-side against a schema

backups.restore_test: verified within the 7 days preceding each cycle's first interview stage
backups.note: An untested backup is not a backup.

privacy.minimum_collection: Do not collect CNIC, date of birth or home address unless a specific process step requires it.
privacy.purpose_limitation: Recruitment data is not used for mailing lists. Marketing consent is a separate, explicit, opt-in checkbox.

retention.then: automatic anonymisation - scores and aggregates retained for year-over-year analysis, identities stripped
retention.rationale: Institutional memory without an ever-growing pile of student PII.

privacy.subject_rights: Any applicant may request their own data export or deletion via their token link.
privacy.exports: Audited and watermarked with the exporting user's identity. Score exports are Super Admin only.
privacy.display_board: IDs only, no names. A public screen of names is an avoidable privacy leak and, in a room full of students who know each other, a source of unnecessary social pressure. The ID is on their slip and their phone; that is enough.
privacy.logs: Structured logs must not contain raw tokens, passwords or CV content.

design_system.source: Generated with the ui-ux-pro-max skill, then corrected where its output conflicted with its own rules or with this product.
design_system.style_rationale: KPI cards, tables, minimal padding, maximum data visibility. Correct for an operations tool.

skill_output_overrides.skill_output: Enterprise Gateway - hero video, solutions by industry, client logos, Contact Sales
skill_output_overrides.reason: That is a marketing site pattern. Nobody signs up for an internal queue console. Wrong artifact entirely.

The skill's own Common Rules require #0F172A for light-mode body text and #475569 minimum for muted. Blue body text fails both, and at 14px on a phone in a bright hall it is measurably harder to read.

Amber must be reserved for WARNING semantics. This product is a state machine; using one amber for 'primary button' and 'you are offline' would create exactly the confusion we are trying to eliminate.

skill_output_overrides.skill_output: Fira Code headings + Fira Sans body
skill_output_overrides.reason: Fira Sans for ALL interface text. Fira Mono reserved for applicant IDs, clock times and counts. Monospace headings look like a terminal; monospace IDs make SPH-SP26-0042 instantly scannable and stop digits jittering as counters tick.
The single most important decision here, and the skill has no state system. This product is a queue - every screen answers 'what state am I in?'

typography.mono_usage: applicant IDs, clock times, counts only

motion.reduced_motion: honoured - removes pulse and all transitions

design_system.colour_rule: Colour is NEVER the only indicator. Each state carries a distinct icon AND a distinct shape. This is a WCAG requirement and also just correct: about 1 in 12 men has a colour-vision deficiency, which at a university induction is several people in the hall - including, statistically, one of your volunteers.

anti_patterns.why: 200 scans times one tap equals 200 chances to double-tap and 200 wasted seconds
It is not an error; red in front of a nervous applicant reads as 'you have a problem'

anti_patterns.never: Spinner with no context on the applicant page
anti_patterns.why: Someone waiting 40 minutes needs 'we are reconnecting', not an ambiguous circle

anti_patterns.never: A single precise ETA such as '14 minutes'
anti_patterns.why: Read as a promise; every broken promise costs trust

anti_patterns.never: Names on the public display board
anti_patterns.why: Avoidable privacy leak, and social pressure in a room full of peers

anti_patterns.never: Score or rank anywhere an interviewer can see
anti_patterns.why: Destroys independence, the entire point of blind evaluation
An interviewer mid-sentence must never have the screen change under them

anti_patterns.never: A disabled control with no explanation
anti_patterns.why: The user cannot tell whether it is broken or forbidden

screens.name: Applicant status page
screens.stakes: highest - 200 anxious people stare at this for up to an hour

structure_top_to_bottom.detail: SPH-SP26-0042, mono, always visible at top
full width, state-coloured, icon plus one line
position, or ROOM NUMBER when called - the largest thing on screen
estimated range, or the instruction when called
Live - updated just now, or Reconnecting - updated 10:41

states.guidance: Check in at the desk when you arrive
Stay in the building - we'll call you here

states.extra: 'I'm on my way' button, 44px, disabled after use with text changed to 'Extended - 2 extra minutes'

states.guidance: We called and missed you - see the desk

micro_decisions: The CALLED state takes over the whole screen - colour, size, and the only button. Missing your call because the room number sat in a corner is the worst avoidable outcome on the page.
Never show a spinner alone. Every reconnecting state keeps the last known number visible with an explicit timestamp. Blanking the screen on someone in position 3 is cruel.
No other applicant's data appears anywhere - enforced by RLS, not by the template.
The ETA is a range, and if it rises the reason appears with it.

screens.name: Volunteer scanner
screens.context: one-handed, in a queue, under fluorescent light, 15 minutes of training
layout: Header: desk name, day, connection state always visible
Live camera, always running, approx 60 percent of height
Persistent search field by name or ID, 44px, thumb-reachable

result_overlay.content: Not a valid SOPHEP code, plus Search button
Register and check in, primary action

screens.dwell_rationale: Successes auto-clear so the volunteer never taps. Failures require dismissal, because a failure that scrolls past unnoticed becomes a person nobody checked in.
screens.offline_banner: Persistent, amber, striped, live pending count, tappable to list pending items. This is the difference between a volunteer who trusts the device and one who starts keeping a paper list in parallel out of anxiety.

states.content: One enormous Call Next button, minimum 56px tall, waiting count for this track, parked count if any. Nothing else, so a tired interviewer cannot mis-tap into something destructive.
Applicant name and ID, visible grace countdown, two large well-separated actions: Start and Mark absent. No confirmation on Start.

Profile and answers left, rubric right. Each criterion shows anchors INLINE - you should not have to remember what 3 means. Elapsed timer against target, amber past target, never blocking. Submit disabled until every criterion is scored, with missing ones marked inline.
Shows exactly WHO has not submitted, plus the Coordinator waiver action. Call Next unavailable, and the screen says WHY in one sentence - never a greyed-out button with no explanation.

screens.name: Coordinator operations dashboard

rows.content: KPI strip: Waiting, In interview, Completed, Parked, Panels open
ACTION REQUIRED - red/amber. Flagged panels with no heartbeat, parked applicants needing location, outstanding evaluations by name, tracks with no open panel, delivery bounces
Live queue, sortable, with per-row priority-bump action
Panels: status, current applicant, elapsed, throughput

screens.key_rule: Action Required is the top of the page and is never empty-by-omission. When there is nothing to do it says so explicitly. A blank area is ambiguous; 'All clear' is information.
screens.usage_guidance: If Action Required is empty and panels are busy, the system is working and you should be talking to applicants, not looking at a screen.

screens.name: Public display board
screens.content: NOW CALLING, then ID to ROOM pairs, then waiting count and average wait
constraints: Large mono type readable at 15 metres
No animation beyond a gentle fade on change - motion on a wall screen in peripheral vision distracts everyone waiting

requirements: Contrast at least 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI boundaries
Every state carries an icon and a shape, not only a colour
Touch targets at least 44x44px with at least 8px gaps
Visible focus rings; full keyboard operation of every staff screen
role='alert' on scan results and errors so screen readers announce them
prefers-reduced-motion removes the pulse and all transitions
Correct inputmode on every field: tel for phone, email for email, numeric for ID search
Renders without horizontal scroll at 375px, 768px, 1024px and 1440px

requirements_summary.could_policy: No requirement is classified Could. Anything that did not earn Must or Should was removed during authoring rather than retained as aspiration - an unprioritised requirement is one nobody will verify.

verification_methods.I: Inspection - code, schema or config review
verification_methods.A: Analysis - load test, model or calculation

definition_of_done: Verification evidence recorded against the stated method
Traceability link to architecture section and flow diagram confirmed accurate
For any Must requirement, no known defect remains open
requirements_summary.full_document: See SOPHEP-RMS-TRD-001 for all 238 requirement statements with priority, verification method and traceability.

key_performance_targets.metric: QR decode latency, camera frame to decoded payload
End-to-end check-in, code presented to confirmation displayed
Real-time propagation, commit to client render
Applicant status page LCP on throttled 3G
Ops dashboard initial render, 500 queue entries

key_performance_targets.target: 250 applicant sessions, 30 staff sessions, 10 panels, 4 check-in devices

key_performance_targets.metric: Applicants per cycle without architectural change
Queue claim latency degradation, 50 to 1000 waiting entries
RPO during an active interview stage
Untrained volunteer completes first successful check-in

scale_path.architecture: Add read replica for analytics; queue index already correct
Shard applicant_seq into 8 counters per cycle (ID becomes SPH-SP26-3-0041); partition audit_events by month
society_id on every root table; RLS extended to society scope; per-society Ed25519 keys

does_not_need_to_change: The queue claim query - SKIP LOCKED scales with panels, not applicants

recommended.why: One codebase for public form, staff app, applicant view, display board

recommended.choice: PWA with IndexedDB and service worker

recommended.why: RLS, SKIP LOCKED, JSONB, sequences - every primitive this design depends on
Postgres-native; RLS applies to subscriptions automatically

recommended.choice: Supabase Auth for staff, custom token flow for applicants
Supabase Storage or Cloudflare R2, private buckets

recommended.why: Already in the plan; good deliverability
Avoids adding Redis for a workload this size
Preview deployments per PR; free at this scale
You need to know about errors DURING the event, not after

recommended.choice: zxing-wasm with native BarcodeDetector where available
recommended.why: Avoid heavy JS-only libraries - scan latency is the single biggest factor in desk throughput

alternative.tradeoff: Same architecture, more operational work. Only choose it if someone on the team will genuinely maintain it after they graduate - which is the real constraint in a student society, and worth being honest about.

build_phases.name: Event core
build_phases.ships: YOU CAN RUN INTERVIEW DAY - the minimum viable induction

phasing_guidance.three_week_scenario: Build Phases 1 and 2, run scoring on paper for one cycle, add Phases 3-4 before the next induction.
phasing_guidance.hard_rule: Do NOT skip Phase 2's queue engine to build the scoring UI first. The queue is what makes the day survivable, and it is the one part you cannot improvise on the floor.

strategy.method: Automated tests over the full transition matrix, including rejection of undefined transitions
Load test at 20 concurrent actors asserting zero duplicate IDs and zero double assignments
Scripted network-partition test, 8-hour buffer, replay reconciliation assertion
Automated per-role per-endpoint matrix test asserting 403 for every denied capability
Direct database test BYPASSING the API, asserting zero rows for unauthorised context
Golden-dataset tests with fixed expected output; determinism verified by repeated runs
Automated axe scan plus manual keyboard and screen-reader pass
Load test at the NFR-SCAL-001 profile
Timed observation with three untrained participants

testing.coverage_target: >= 80 percent for state transition logic, queue claim path, scoring computation and allocation
critical_test_cases: 20 concurrent registrations produce 20 distinct IDs with no gaps from contention
20 concurrent Call Next requests produce 20 distinct applicants
Same QR scanned twice on two devices produces one check_in row
Recusal table containing a NULL does not suppress the queue
Allocation run twice over identical input produces byte-identical output
Interviewer A cannot SELECT interviewer B's evaluation via direct SQL with A's RLS context
Unset RLS context returns zero rows, never all rows
Same Super Admin cannot both lock and confirm
Offline check-in for 8 hours then reconnect yields 100 percent reconciliation, zero duplicates
Stage close blocked while an interview is in_progress
Panel cannot Call Next while awaiting_evaluations
Wait estimate rises with a stated cause when a panel closes

risks.risk: Evaluations not submitted by end of day

risks.mitigation: Zero-tap success path (FR-CHK-002), non-error styling for expected conditions (NFR-USE-004)
Deterministic allocation (FR-DEC-007), append-only audit (FR-AUD-003), Auditor role (FR-RBAC-009)

risks.risk: Device loss or theft during event
risks.mitigation: No secrets on device (FR-IDT-007), roster contains hashes only (FR-CHK-018)
Configuration over code (NFR-MAIN-001), documentation, versioned migrations
Blind evaluation (FR-INT-004), shrinkage (FR-SCR-002), disagreement flagging (FR-SCR-007), recusal (FR-INT-017)
Row-level policy (FR-RBAC-005), no names on display (NFR-PRIV-006), retention limit (NFR-PRIV-003)

constraints.constraint: The system is maintained by student volunteers with turnover at graduation. Operational complexity is a first-order cost, not a secondary concern.
Campus network reliability cannot be assumed at any point during an event.
Volunteers receive at most 15 minutes of training, on the day.
No third-party service may sit in the synchronous path of check-in, queue claim or evaluation submission.
Budget assumes free or education-tier hosting; the architecture must remain within those limits at 1000 applicants.
Interviewer availability is the binding throughput constraint and is outside system control.

assumptions.if_false: Manual search and printed slips already cover this; no change

assumptions.assumption: One general interview round is sufficient
assumptions.if_false: Second-round UI required; schema already supports it via queue_entries.round
Throughput model and capacity screen require recalibration

assumptions.assumption: Departments have fixed capacities before allocation
assumptions.if_false: Allocation cannot run; FR-DEC-003 blocks it by design
Wait estimate seed and capacity model require reconfiguration only

assumptions.assumption: Venue has mains power for the display board and desks

open_issues.impact: Drives throughput more than any other variable

open_issues.issue: One general interview, or one per department preference
open_issues.default: one general, department fit as a rubric criterion plus recommendation

open_issues.issue: May an applicant be placed in more than one department
Is a second interview round required
open_issues.impact: UI scope; schema already supports it

open_issues.issue: Publication: individual notices only, or also a public list of selected identifiers

open_issues.impact: Seeds wait estimation and the capacity model

open_issues.issue: Waiver authority: Coordinator or Super Admin
Confirmed hosting tier and data residency
Whether faculty approval is required for the data retention policy

Departments, capacities and rubric versions confirmed and locked
All interviewers have logged in at least once and completed TOTP setup

v2_corrected.name: Permission Gate, Role Union and Fail-Closed RLS

figma_artifacts.known_quirk: v2-11 contains a deliberate loop DECISIONS to OFFERS to DECISIONS. This represents the waitlist cascade creating a new decision version when an offer lapses. It is real, not a modelling slip, but it reads oddly cold.

decisions_changed_from_user_original.reason: Spring 2026 and Fall 2026 produced identical prefixes; two cycles in one year collided semantically
Two registration desks using SELECT MAX+1 WILL produce duplicates - the most common bug in systems like this

decisions_changed_from_user_original.changed_to: Every applicant gets a token; QR is one rendering of it
decisions_changed_from_user_original.reason: Two divergent check-in paths and a second-class experience for walk-ins; volunteers must remember which flow applies

decisions_changed_from_user_original.changed_to: Full HTTPS URL with an Ed25519 signature
decisions_changed_from_user_original.reason: Correct instinct, but a bare token requires a custom scanner. A URL means any phone camera works as a fallback, and asymmetric signing enables safe offline verification

decisions_changed_from_user_original.changed_to: Pull model - panels claim when free
decisions_changed_from_user_original.reason: Push assignment goes stale the moment one interview runs long; the applicant is told Room 2 while Room 2 is 20 minutes behind
A single queue routes people to panels that cannot evaluate them while specialist interviewers sit idle

decisions_changed_from_user_original.changed_to: EWMA over active panels, displayed as a range with honest upward revision
decisions_changed_from_user_original.reason: A naive estimate that jumps around destroys trust faster than showing nothing
Raw averaging silently rewards applicants who drew lenient interviewers

decisions_changed_from_user_original.changed_to: Full decision pipeline through allocation, offers and waitlist
decisions_changed_from_user_original.reason: The hardest part was missing - turning scores into placements under capacity constraints

decisions_changed_from_user_original.changed_to: Real-time as an enhancement layer over an offline-capable core
decisions_changed_from_user_original.reason: If the socket drops, the event must continue

decisions_changed_from_user_original.changed_to: Added Coordinator and Auditor; dual control on publication
decisions_changed_from_user_original.reason: No floor manager, no read-only auditor, and one person could unilaterally publish results
